zh: 我知道听起来怎样,但,是的,我想,你知道,在欧洲做移民大概给了我很多肩上的负担,很多要向自己和世界证明的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this probably comes from there, I would guess, or maybe it's just genetic.
zh: 所以我猜这可能源于此,或者也许就是基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows?
zh: 谁知道呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a CEO, you learn very quickly that probably the number one traits that
zh: 但作为 CEO,你很快就会学到,大概排在第一位的、

speaker: Unknown
en: is terrible for a CEO is if they're conflict-averse.
zh: 对 CEO 来说很糟糕的特质,就是他们回避冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I learned that very quickly, that conflict-averse CEOs is like the worst thing possible.
zh: 所以我很快就学到了,回避冲突的 CEO 是最糟糕的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's nothing worse than that.
zh: 没有比这更糟的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not saying they're bad people.
zh: 我不是说他们是坏人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're wonderful people.
zh: 他们是很棒的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, in fact, maybe the most wonderful people in the world are conflict-averse, right?
zh: 就像,事实上,也许世界上最棒的人恰恰是回避冲突的人,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But the CEO job...
zh: 但 CEO 这份工作……

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be crystal clear.
zh: 你必须非常清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason is, I think that, you know, everybody's pushing you, right?
zh: 原因是,我觉得,你知道,每个人都在推你,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody wants to get something from you.
zh: 每个人都想从你这里得到点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you do this?
zh: 就因为你在电梯里和我闲聊,我对你很客气,你也对我很客气,现在你就想硬塞进某个东西的批准,你这招真的很阴。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you prove that?
zh: 你能证明那个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we do this?
zh: 我们能做这个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're conflict diverse, you're just going to say yes to them, or you're going to lie to them, or you're going to try to avoid the subject.
zh: 如果你回避冲突,你就只会对他们说好,或者对他们撒谎,或者试图避开这个话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to be crystal clear.
zh: 你必须非常清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't do that here.
zh: 我们这里不这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no.
zh: 就是不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no, we're not going to do that.
zh: 就是不,我们不会那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I'm not going to prove because you caught me in the hallway here.
zh: 不,我不会去证明,就因为你在走廊里碰到了我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go through the formal processes.
zh: 走正式流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just because you're chit-chatting with me in the elevator and I'm being nice and you're being nice back, and now you're trying to jam in approval for something, that's really sneaky of you.
zh: 只是因为你在电梯里和我闲聊，我对你很友善，你也友善地回应，然后你就想趁机塞进某个东西的审批，你这样做真的很阴。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's go through the proper process for this.
zh: 所以我们按正规流程来办这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all this push all the time, if you don't do it, the companies start going in all kinds of directions instead of laser focusing all that energy on that one bottleneck that you wanted to solve, right?
zh: 所以这种推力一直都有,如果你不这么做,公司就会开始往各种方向走,而不是把所有能量激光式地聚焦在你想解决的那一个瓶颈上,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think that it helps you be more consistent and clear, so everybody kind of gets the message.
zh: 我也觉得这能帮你保持更一致、更清晰,这样每个人都能接收到同样的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: People don't understand nuance.
zh: 人们理解不了微妙之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Ali meant this.
zh: 我觉得 Ali 指的是这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, no, I think he meant that.
zh: 不,不,不,我觉得他指的是那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, I think you're totally misunderstanding him.
zh: 不,不,我觉得你完全误解他了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's be crystal clear then.
zh: 那我们就说得非常清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's make it black and white so that there's no doubt.
zh: 我们把它变成非黑即白,这样就没有疑问了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everybody knows.
zh: 这样每个人都知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's give them the cheat sheet.
zh: 我们给他们一份速查表。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, you got to be aggressive with that.
zh: 所以,你知道,你必须在这点上很强势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you start getting people that are more like-minded and you kind of start growing in the same direction.
zh: 然后你开始吸引到更多志同道合的人,你们就开始朝着同一个方向成长。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like big companies otherwise, like we're 12,000 employees, it's like they start canceling each other out, atoms bouncing off of each other, you know, strategies that don't make sense.
zh: 我觉得大公司不然的话,比如我们有一万两千名员工,就会开始互相抵消,像原子一样互相碰撞,你知道的,一些毫无道理的战略。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw it in big companies, so I'm trying to avoid that, you know, really.
zh: 我在大公司里见过这些,所以我真的在努力避免那种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just pulling on that thread, I have a thesis, and I think you agree with it, is a pivot point in a lot of startups is when you get to 150 employees, Dunbar's number, and things start to really slow down.
zh: 顺着这个话题说下去,我有一个论点,我想你也同意,就是很多初创公司的一个转折点是当你达到 150 名员工的时候,也就是邓巴数,然后一切开始明显慢下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys hit 150, and then, you know, you're 12,000 today.
zh: 你们达到了 150,然后,你知道,你们今天已经一万两千人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree with that?
zh: 你同意那个说法吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So many of the companies I work with are ripping by that 150.
zh: 我合作的很多公司都在 150 这个坎上挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your advice to founders to create some structure and process, but not really slow the damn thing down?
zh: 你对创始人有什么建议,既能建立一些结构和流程,又不会真的把这个该死的东西拖慢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, some slowdown is sort of necessary.
zh: 是的,一定程度的放慢是某种必要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number number definitely happened.
zh: 那个数字数字确实发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt, for us, I felt like it was like 250 or something, but you're right.
zh: 我感觉，对我们来说，好像是 250 左右，但你说得对。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was around the time, actually, we did the CEO transition, right?
zh: 实际上那大概是在我们做 CEO 交接的时候，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it goes from being everybody knows everyone, and you as a CEO know everything that's going on.
zh: 我觉得它从一个所有人都认识所有人、而你作为 CEO 知道正在发生的一切的状态转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in some sense, you can run the company.
zh: 所以在某种意义上，你可以一个人运营这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of like a star like you know there's like one person that knows everything or two people that knows everything and then there's a bunch of people around but you know everything so you have to start putting structure in place so that you know you don't know everything you just trust that you know this part of the go-to-market will take care of itself this part of so you have to basically start
zh: 有点像一个中心，你知道，就像有一个人知道所有事情，或者两个人知道所有事情，然后周围有一群人，但你知道一切，所以你必须开始建立结构，这样，你知道，你不再知道所有事情，你只是相信这一部分的市场推广会自己运转好，这一部分会，所以你基本上必须开始

speaker: Unknown
en: Putting in processes where you're scaling indirectly.
zh: 建立流程，让公司在间接扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in a way, I know it sounds funny because I'm sure you have managers and managers of managers, but really it's the first time the company is going through the transition of you have managers of managers.
zh: 在某种程度上，我知道这听起来好笑，因为我确信你有经理和经理的经理，但这真的是公司第一次经历“出现经理的经理”的转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: They might have had it before, but those managers of managers didn't matter because the CEO knew everything anyway.
zh: 以前可能有过，但那些经理的经理并不重要，因为 CEO 反正知道一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they were just managers of managers in name.
zh: 所以他们只是名义上的经理的经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what happens when you actually can't reach down because there's like too many people, you actually can't reach down and understand what's going on.
zh: 但当你真的够不着基层时会发生什么，因为人太多了，你真的够不下去了解正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You really have to go through.
zh: 你真的必须经过。

speaker: Unknown
en: The intermediate layer, you've got to put structure in place and make sure that everything reviews, KPIs, measure it in a way so that you can make sure that the ship is going in the direction you want it to without going and tapping people's shoulders all the time because there's too many shoulders now.
zh: 中间那层，你必须建立结构，确保一切都有评审、KPI，以某种方式去衡量，这样你就能确保这艘船朝着你想要的方向前进，而不必总是去拍人们的肩膀，因为现在肩膀太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't even know the name of everyone anymore.
zh: 你甚至不再知道每个人的名字了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've also interviewed Jack Dorsey on this podcast and I read a lot about Brian Armstrong.
zh: 我也在这档播客上采访过 Jack Dorsey，而且我读了很多关于 Brian Armstrong 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're trying to recreate the CEO model and rethink it.
zh: 他们都在试图重塑 CEO 模式并重新思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way Dorsey kind of describes it is the company is an AI and the employees kind of sit around the AI and their main job is to train the AI and give it context over time.
zh: Dorsey 的描述方式大概是：公司就是一个 AI，员工们围绕在这个 AI 周围，他们的主要工作是随时间训练这个 AI 并给它提供上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that he wants no more than two layers between himself and the frontline employees.
zh: 而且他希望自己和一线员工之间不超过两层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Brian Armstrong's doing kind of similar things, like not just shrinking the org, but really collapsing the number of levels in the org.
zh: Brian Armstrong 在做类似的事情，不只是缩减组织，而是真正压缩组织里的层级数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your take?
zh: 你的看法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like there's a movement starting around this.
zh: 围绕这个似乎正在兴起一场运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a bunch of the AI native companies I'm working with are pretty intrigued by that.
zh: 而且我合作的一批 AI 原生公司对此相当感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think directional is correct.
zh: 是的，我认为大方向是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're doing the same.
zh: 我们也在做同样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we should separate two things that are, I think a little bit sometimes being conflated.
zh: 但我认为我们应该区分两件，我觉得有时候会被混为一谈的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the official org chart you want to have in a company?
zh: 一是你想在公司里拥有什么样的正式组织架构图？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what is the way in which your company disseminates information, aggregates information, makes decisions and collects those?
zh: 然后是你的公司传播信息、汇总信息、做决策并收集这些的方式是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We should separate these two.
zh: 我们应该把这两者分开。

speaker: Unknown
en: So 10, 20 years ago, these were the same thing.
zh: 在 10 年、20 年前，这两者是同一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is no way to collect information other than, you know, you ask your person, they ask their people, like you kind of, you know, so you go up and down.
zh: 除了，你知道，你问你的下属，他们再去问他们的下属，没有别的收集信息的方式，你知道，就是那种，你在树上上下往返。

speaker: Unknown
en: The tree structure of the org chart.
zh: 组织架构图的树状结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how information disseminates up and down and decisions go up and down.
zh: 信息就是这样上下传播，决策也是这样上下流动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the only way.
zh: 那是唯一的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do it more broadcast, that's like a top-down company, or you can do bottom-up, but those are the only options you have.
zh: 你可以做得更广播一点，那就像一个自上而下的公司，或者你可以自下而上，但那是你仅有的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you can just be random, poorly run company.
zh: 或者你也可以就做一个随意的、运营很烂的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, what has happened is that we have extremely smart AI.
zh: 今天，发生的事情是我们拥有了极其聪明的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I keep asking this question every audience I go to, and I ask them, you know, how many of you think that the AI is smarter than most of the people around you most of the time?
zh: 我每到一个场合都反复问这个问题，我问他们，你知道，你们当中有多少人认为 AI 在大多数时候比你们周围的大多数人都聪明？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I get like 90% of the hands up.
zh: 然后大概 90% 的人举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I define that as AGI.
zh: 好吧，我把那个定义为 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's artificial general intelligence.
zh: 人工通用智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might not be super intelligence.
zh: 它可能还不是超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it is as good as most of the people around you, right?
zh: 但它已经和你周围的大多数人一样好了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is undisputed.
zh: 这是无可争议的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time I ask this, audiences all agree on that.
zh: 每次我问这个问题，听众都同意这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't agree that AGI is here because they have a weird definition of AGI.
zh: 他们不同意 AGI 已经到来，是因为他们对 AGI 有一个奇怪的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have these models that are super, super smart.
zh: 所以我们有了这些超级、超级聪明的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we look at how AI is being used inside corporations.
zh: 然后我们看看 AI 在企业内部是如何被使用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, people complain about them hallucinating, but humans hallucinate too.
zh: 顺便说一句，人们抱怨它们产生幻觉，但人类也会产生幻觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I make mistakes all the time.
zh: 我一直在犯错。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the time.
zh: 一直都在。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know?
zh: 你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So these things are phenomenal already.
zh: 所以这些东西已经非常惊人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's just say they're smarter than most of the people around you most of the time is what I've gone from every... By the way, I asked that at Moscone Center to 32,000 people and I asked them to raise their hands and almost everybody raised their hands.
zh: 我就直说了，它们大多数时候比你周围的大多数人都聪明，这是我从每一次……顺便说一句，我在 Moscone Center 向 32,000 个人问了这个问题，我请他们举手，几乎所有人都举了手。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you look around you and say, okay, what's happening inside the enterprise?
zh: 但然后你环顾四周，说，好吧，企业内部到底发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: How are AI being used?
zh: AI 是怎么被使用的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're just using them as stupid chatbots.
zh: 他们只是把它们当作愚蠢的聊天机器人来用。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to the chatbot, asking it the question and getting an answer.
zh: 他们打开聊天机器人，问它问题，然后得到一个答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's all that's happening.
zh: 发生的就只有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they're using them for coding.
zh: 然后他们还用它们来写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they have a coding agents that are writing code.
zh: 所以他们有写代码的 coding agents。

speaker: Unknown
en: By and large, it's a little bit of an oversimplification.
zh: 总的来说，这有点过于简化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what's happening inside the enterprise today.
zh: 这就是如今企业内部正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: This huge gap between the capabilities the models have and, you know, it is just not true.
zh: 模型的能力和……之间存在着巨大的鸿沟，你知道，情况就是这样，这是事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked this question too.
zh: 我也问过这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have hundreds of agentic coworkers collaborating with each other, providing proposals to you, keeping you up to date and doing that?
zh: 你们有没有数百个 agentic 的同事在彼此协作、向你们提交提案、让你们随时了解最新情况，做着这些事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody raises their hand.
zh: 没有人举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never had a single person raise their hand on that.
zh: 我从来没有见过任何一个人在这个问题上举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's lacking is the enterprise context.
zh: 所以缺的是企业上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need to capture the enterprise context that's in people's heads, decisions that are being made every day, what's happening inside every meeting that's being recorded, every email that's being sent.
zh: 所以你需要捕捉存在于人们头脑中的企业上下文，每天都在做出的决策，每一次被录制的会议中发生了什么，每一封被发出的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything has to be captured and be put part of the context and then fed to the AI.
zh: 所有东西都必须被捕捉，成为上下文的一部分，然后喂给 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call this an ontology.
zh: 我们把这称为本体(ontology)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want to capture the ontology and feed it to the AI.
zh: 所以我们想捕捉这个本体，并把它喂给 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually built a product that does that.
zh: 所以我们实际上构建了一个做这件事的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called Genie.
zh: 它叫 Genie。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for Databricks, so it's not just buy this product and you will solve this problem and you're done.
zh: 而对于 Databricks 来说，这并不是说买了这个产品你就能解决这个问题，然后就完事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, absolutely not.
zh: 不，绝对不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out you have to also build this ontology.
zh: 结果发现你还必须构建这个本体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Databricks, we actually have a phenomenal ontology we built for ourselves.
zh: 而在 Databricks,我们实际上为自己构建了一个非常出色的本体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've noticed our customers don't have, they use the same product, but they haven't built up the ontology the same way we have.
zh: 我们注意到我们的客户没有，他们用的是同样的产品，但他们没有像我们这样把本体建立起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us now, it's magical.
zh: 所以对我们来说，现在这就像魔法一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have an org chart of people, they report up and down, and we can decide what the fan out should be and spans of control and all of that.
zh: 所以我们有一个人员的组织架构图，有上下级汇报关系，我们可以决定扇出应该是多少，管理幅度是多少，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we have Genie and Genie pretty much answers any question I have in any meeting about anything.
zh: 然后我们有 Genie,Genie 几乎能回答我在任何会议中关于任何事情的任何问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it can also start automating tasks for us and getting us, you know, so we're all just sitting on our phones and using the Genie app all the time on all of these kinds of things and feeding more context to it, building up more context, automating more and more processes in the company that we find.
zh: 它还能开始为我们自动化任务，帮我们……你知道，我们所有人都只是坐在那里用手机，一直在用 Genie 应用处理所有这类事情，给它喂更多上下文，建立更多上下文，把我们发现的公司里越来越多的流程自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, I think it's true that the Genie product does this and builds the ontology.
zh: 所以，是的，我认为 Genie 这个产品确实做到了这一点，构建了本体。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then what about the humans?
zh: 但那么人类呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about that pyramid shaped org chart?
zh: 那个金字塔形状的组织架构图呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that that is TBD, and here's why, where I think there's a lot of stuff that's being said in the market that I'm not sure is correct.

en: Is the value software zero?
zh: 软件的价值是零吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's like, no, but why is revenue going?
zh: 也许是这样，不对，可为什么营收在下滑？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, revenue is accelerating?
zh: 哦，营收在加速增长？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, this should be high.
zh: 哦，这个应该很高才对。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we just want to avoid that.
zh: 所以我们只是想避免那种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think things will settle in in a year or so.
zh: 我觉得事情会在一年左右稳定下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've used the word bullshit and bullshit detector a bunch, and you talked about being comfortable with conflict.
zh: 你多次用到「胡扯」和「胡扯探测器」这两个词，你还谈到要习惯冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just say you're not comfortable with the conflict and you're a normal homo sapien and you become a CEO and it's starting to scale.
zh: 假设你不习惯冲突，你是个正常的智人，你成了一名 CEO，公司开始扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you develop that bullshit detector and use it?
zh: 你怎么培养那种胡扯探测器并加以运用？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you get used to this conflict?
zh: 还有你怎么适应这种冲突？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's unnatural for most people.
zh: 因为对大多数人来说这是反本能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, don't lie to yourself.
zh: 嗯，不要欺骗自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's the most important thing.
zh: 你知道，这是最重要的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like a lot of people lie to themselves.
zh: 我觉得很多人都在欺骗自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't tell themselves what's wrong with the company, what's wrong with it.
zh: 他们不告诉自己公司哪里出了问题，问题到底是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: When they come up with excuses, self-defense mechanisms get in the way and they say, well, you know, they find excuses.
zh: 当他们找借口时，自我防御机制就会作祟，他们会说，嗯，你知道，他们会找各种借口。

speaker: Unknown
en: So start seeing the truth of what's actually not working with individuals or the company or your strategy.
zh: 所以，要开始看清真相——不管是个人、公司还是你的战略，到底是什么在失灵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you want to take truth seeking to its extreme, you can't be conflict diverse about it.
zh: 而且如果你想追求真相到底，你就不能回避冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of have to face and challenge that
zh: 你必须直面并挑战

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, that gap, that discrepancy, head on.
zh: 你知道，那个差距、那个偏差，正面迎上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't swallow that.
zh: 不要吞下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just go after it.
zh: 就去追着它干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, be aggressive about it and push yourself.
zh: 就是，要主动出击，逼自己一把。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, okay, hey, Ali, you're not conflict-averse.
zh: 就像，好吧，嘿，Ali，你不回避冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people are conflict-averse.
zh: 有些人是回避冲突的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's kind of like saying, oh, you know, some people, they don't like to go to the gym and work out because it's, like, too annoying.
zh: 嗯，这就好比说，哦，你知道，有些人不喜欢去健身房锻炼，因为这，太烦了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But other people, they just seem to have this gene that makes them work out.
zh: 但另一些人，他们似乎天生就有一种让他们去锻炼的基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's hard for everyone.
zh: 不，对每个人来说都很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sucks for everyone to go to the gym and work out or eat healthy or do these things.
zh: 对每个人来说，去健身房锻炼、或者吃得健康、或者做这些事都很痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet we push ourselves.
zh: 但我们还是逼自己去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, maybe it's slightly easier.
zh: 现在，也许对某些人来说稍微容易一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe some people have more motivation.
zh: 也许有些人动力更强。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easier to push themselves.
zh: 逼自己更容易一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe some people have an act for it.
zh: 也许有些人有这方面的天赋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe for some people it's harder, but I think I put it in that category that you should, you know, eat your vegetables and you should live a healthy life.
zh: 也许对有些人来说更难，但我觉得应该把它归入那一类——你应该，你知道，吃你的蔬菜，你应该过健康的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that the natural thing is just to eat a bunch of sugar and like, you know, just sit back and do nothing.
zh: 而人的本性就是吃一堆糖，然后，你知道，就瘫着什么都不干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're, if you're conflict diverse, get over yourself.
zh: 所以如果你，如果你回避冲突，克服你自己的这一套。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, get over it.
zh: 是的，克服它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, if you want to be CEO, you do not want to be a CEO.
zh: 就是，如果你想当 CEO——你不想当 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to be CEO, don't say I'm a conflict.
zh: 如果你想当 CEO，不要说我是个回避冲突的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Change that.
zh: 改掉它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, don't say, hey, I want to be an athlete, but I'm the kind of athlete that doesn't work out.
zh: 就像，不要说，嘿，我想当运动员，但我是那种不锻炼的运动员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because, you know, in my family, we don't work out.
zh: 因为，你知道，在我们家，我们不锻炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we don't practice.
zh: 所以我们不练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't work out.
zh: 我们不锻炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: The results are not great, but I'm not the kind that works out and is healthy and eats healthy food.
zh: 成绩不怎么样，但我不是那种会锻炼、身体健康、吃得健康的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm the other kind.
zh: 我是另一种。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, that doesn't.
zh: 不，那不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to be in the sport, this is the name of the game.
zh: 如果你想干这行，这就是这个游戏的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you got to be crystal clear with people and you have to tackle the conflicts head on.
zh: 就是说，你必须对人们非常透明，并且你必须正面迎击冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't love the conflicts.
zh: 我并不喜欢冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who likes the conflict?
zh: 谁喜欢冲突呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say it's human to hate conflict.
zh: 我想说，讨厌冲突是人的天性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's unpleasant.
zh: 它让人不愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a conflict means someone pushes back, they're unhappy, they might criticize you back.
zh: 冲突意味着有人反驳你，他们不高兴，他们可能反过来批评你。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not pleasant.
zh: 这不令人愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody likes that.
zh: 没人喜欢那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a human thing to not like conflict.
zh: 不喜欢冲突是人的天性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, some people really avoid it.
zh: 不过，有些人会特别回避它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people avoid it less, but get over it if you're a CEO.
zh: 有些人回避得少一些，但如果你是 CEO,就得克服它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ali, thanks for coming on.
zh: Ali,感谢你来参加节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congratulations on all your success.
zh: 祝贺你取得的所有成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were fantastic.
zh: 你太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Appreciate all the wisdom you've dropped on the crowd.
zh: 感谢你分享给听众的所有智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Likewise.
zh: 彼此彼此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pleasure to talk to you and saw you do similar things at HubSpot.
zh: 和你聊天很愉快，我看你在 HubSpot 也做着类似的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thanks for having me on.
zh: 所以感谢你邀请我来。

speaker: Unknown
en: My pleasure.
zh: 我的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hope everyone liked that interview with Ali.
zh: 希望大家喜欢那期对 Ali 的访谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he's fantastic.
zh: 我觉得他非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: A couple of my takeaways.
zh: 说几点我的收获。

speaker: Unknown
en: First is kind of a vibe takeaway.
zh: 第一点算是一种气质层面的收获。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, don't be a wuss is sort of a piece of his CEO advice.
zh: 就是说，“别当软蛋”算是他给 CEO 建议的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he reminds me a lot.
zh: 他让我想起很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I interviewed Nikesh Arora from Palo Alto.
zh: 我采访过 Palo Alto 的 Nikesh Arora。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, they don't put up with any BS.
zh: 就是说，他们不容忍任何胡扯。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have strong BS detectors.
zh: 他们有很强的胡扯探测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: They use those BS detectors.
zh: 他们会使用那些胡扯探测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: They both believe that conflict aversion is kind of cancer in a CEO, and I suspect they're right about that.
zh: 他们都认为回避冲突对 CEO 来说算是一种癌症，我怀疑他们是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And neither over-indexes on being liked.
zh: 而且两人都不过度在意被人喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was CEO of HubSpot, I think I did over-index on it.
zh: 我当 HubSpot CEO 的时候，我想我确实过度在意这个了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We won all those Glassdoor prizes back in the day.
zh: 我们当年拿遍了那些 Glassdoor 奖项。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure that's correlated with long-term success.
zh: 我不确定那和长期成功有相关性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did pretty well long-term, but I think I over-indexed on it.
zh: 我们长期做得相当不错，但我觉得我在这一点上过度在意了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you look at like Steve Jobs and these guys, they definitely don't.
zh: 你看像 Steve Jobs 和这些家伙，他们绝对不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of not being a wuss,
zh: 说到不当软蛋，

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to have the courage of your convictions and you have to have staying power on that conviction.
zh: 你必须对自己的信念有勇气，并且你必须在这份信念上保持持久力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, conviction without staying power is like a fad diet in January.
zh: 你知道，没有持久力的信念就像一月份的流行节食法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just doesn't work.
zh: 它就是行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the best conviction is kind of, there's an old saying, you need to be right about something that everyone thinks you're wrong about.
zh: 而最好的信念是，有句老话说，你需要在一个所有人都认为你错的事情上被证明是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that happens to be true and you're convicted and patient with it, that's where the big, big outcomes come from.
zh: 如果事实恰好如此，而你对此坚信不疑并有耐心，那就是那些巨大的、巨大的成果的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, a lot of people talk about conviction around the founding idea.
zh: 很多人谈的是围绕创立最初想法的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: I found, because I mostly work with scale up CEOs, that conviction around second acts is even more important than conviction around the first idea.
zh: 我发现，因为我主要和规模化阶段的 CEO 合作，围绕“第二幕”的信念甚至比围绕第一个想法的信念更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Ali did this a couple of times, but he talked the most about a product he launched a few years called Lakehouse, which was sort of a big competitive offering.
zh: Ali 做到过几次，但他谈得最多的是他几年前发布的一款叫 Lakehouse 的产品，那算是一个大型的竞争性产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was unique in the market.
zh: 它在市场上是独一无二的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone thought he was wrong about it, including most of his employees, and he really, really just stuck to it.
zh: 所有人都认为他在这件事上错了，包括他的大多数员工，而他真的、真的就是坚持了下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had a lot of conviction and patience with it, and it paid off over a long period of time.
zh: 他对此有很多信念和耐心，长期来看得到了回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in a board meeting yesterday with one of my CEOs, and they've got an application the business is ripping, but they need to move to more of a platform.
zh: 我昨天和一个我投资的 CEO 开董事会，他们有一个应用业务正在快速起飞，但他们需要转型成更多平台化的形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be a very difficult shift.
zh: 这会是一次非常艰难的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's going to get a lot of pushback.
zh: 他会遭到很多阻力。

speaker: Unknown
en: His sales organization is really not going to want to sell it.
zh: 他的销售组织真的很不愿意去卖它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the advice I gave him is sort of the advice I gave myself at HubSpot.
zh: 我给他的建议，有点像我在 HubSpot 给自己的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like at scale, those second acts, you need to like swing the pendulum all the way to the other side and get the whole darn company focused on the second act and just over index on it.
zh: 在规模化阶段，那些第二幕转型，你需要把钟摆彻底摆到另一边，让整个公司都聚焦在第二幕上，并且过度投入在其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you're in the middle, people will stick with that old first act.
zh: 因为如果你处于中间状态，人们会继续守着旧的第三幕……旧的第一幕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I see him doing that.
zh: 而我看到他正在这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I liked about what he did was he only had one or two focus areas a year.
zh: 我喜欢他做的地方在于，他一年只有一两个重点领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's very focused.
zh: 他非常专注。

speaker: Unknown
en: He focused on the bottleneck.
zh: 他专注于瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounded like his number one focus for two or three years on his annual plan was that Lakehouse product.
zh: 听起来他两三年来年度计划的第一重点就是那个 Lakehouse 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So over index on the thing you want to change.
zh: 所以，对你想改变的事情要过度投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Changing is harder as you get bigger.
zh: 公司越大，改变越难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so over indexing is really important.
zh: 所以过度投入真的非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope you liked it.
zh: 希望你喜欢这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really enjoyed the interview.
zh: 我真的很享受这次访谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Follow us here if you want to tune into all the long, strange episodes with lots and lots of great CEOs.
zh: 如果你想收听所有这些漫长而奇特的、有非常多优秀 CEO 的节目，请在这里关注我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: See you next time.
zh: 下次见。
